boundary_evidence: NOT FROM tu_map. tools/tu_map.py reports the arm9 `main` module as UNDER-SEGMENTED -- one unit 0x20049f0..0x20707a4 with 2984 functions and 73 class labels -- so there is no tu_map boundary and no `tubuild.py create` candidate id. Every line below is hand-derived.

contiguous run 0x0203b3c0..0x0203b4dc: the four functions tile the span exactly, 0x78 + 0x74 + 0x18 + 0x18 = 0x120 = end-start, no hole and no tail (recomputed from config/arm9/symbols.txt). No foreign symbol lies inside it.
class-label homogeneity is total: both symbols are _ZN7fBase_c9SceneNode*, i.e. members of the nested class fBase_c::SceneNode, and there are no others anywhere in the image.

SEPARATE FROM ActorBase'S OWN TU, and this is the load-bearing negative. These are the only two _ZN7fBase_c* functions outside the class's main run at 0x02043444..0x02043f4c, and they sit 0x8000 bytes below it. A single object's .text is placed contiguously by the linker, so one TU cannot occupy two regions 0x8000 apart -- merging them into arm9/ActorBase would require exactly that. arm9/ActorBase is independently TEXT-VERIFIED over the full 0x02043444..0x02043f4c run without them, which confirms the split from the other side.

neighbourhood attribution: 0x0203b2xx-0x0203b4xx is the intrusive-list primitive stretch -- func_0203b20c, func_0203b244, func_0203b27c and func_0203b3c0 all live there, and every one of them is called from ActorBase's own members (AfterInitResources, AfterCleanupResources, func_02043880). This pair sits at the TOP of that stretch, which is consistent with a scene-graph-node TU adjacent to the list code it is built on.

neighbours on both sides carry a different label: func_0203b394 ends at 0x0203b3c0 below, and _ZN4cstd5atan2E5Fix12IiES1_ begins at 0x0203b4dc above -- a cstd math routine, which is certainly a different TU.

CONFIDENCE IS medium, NOT high, and the reason is stated rather than hidden: the two list primitives immediately below the members (func_0203b3c0, func_0203b438) are absorbed on contiguity and shared list-node concern -- both operate on the same parent/child/prev/next layout SceneNode::Reset clears, and both are called from fBase_c's own routines -- but they keep their address-given names, so nothing positively proves the original .cpp spelled them as SceneNode members. The lower boundary at 0x0203b3c0 is therefore a floor supported by the stop at func_0203b394, which carries no scene-node affinity. The upper boundary at 0x0203b4dc is strong (a cstd template instantiation cannot share a TU with an actor scene node).

static-initialiser attribution: no help. main has 23 sinits / 23 .ctor entries, sinit_vs_tu 'ok', corroborated=false, and this run touches no dynamically-initialised static storage -- the object emits no .init, no .bss and no .data.

compiler_only_output.reason: mwccarm emits the unused base-object constructor beside the licensed C1; the ROM has no configured C2 home and the surviving methods do not reference it

notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main. The entry was built through tubuild.build_manifest_entry so the schema is the tool's own; boundary_confidence and boundary_evidence were then replaced with hand-derived values.

This is the 0x30-byte OUTLIER of the fBase_c assignment: 25 _ZN7fBase_c* function symbols exist in the image, 23 in the main run (see arm9/ActorBase) and these 2 here. include/fBase_c.h records the split.

Both licensed functions are genuine `fBase_c::SceneNode` member definitions. `SceneNode` is nested in `fBase_c`, and `fBase_c`'s already-existing constructor is declared explicitly so introducing the nested constructor does not change implicit-constructor code generation. The affected-header production sweep compiled 2,124 sources and reproduced all 106 modules exactly.

mwccarm emits the C2 base-object constructor beside the ROM-resident C1. The exact compiler_only_output policy dead-strips C2 because it has no configured ROM home and no surviving reference; the licensed C1 and Reset members remain byte- and relocation-exact. Reset() clears only the first four words and deliberately leaves the owner back-pointer at +0x10 alone; fBase_c's constructor writes that one.
